About the school

Education within reach of every family in the sitio.

Before 2020, the nearest elementary school was about 8 kilometers from Sitio Upper Rancho. The school opened on September 29, 2020 through the work of the district and Bangahan Integrated School, and it continues to operate as an extension of Bangahan Integrated School.

As an extension of Bangahan Integrated School, the school does not yet have its own school ID, so it receives no MOOE (maintenance and operating budget) from the Department of Education. For now, Bangahan Integrated School pays the school's electric and water bills, so these are no longer a burden on our teachers and learners. We are praying for our own school ID and for all the privileges of a school promised by the Department of Education's vision and mission.

Most families here farm corn, rice, sugarcane, coconut and cassava. The school welcomes every child regardless of age, culture, ability, religion or income, and teaches local values alongside the national curriculum.

Our history

From an 8-kilometer walk to a school of our own.

July 2018

The community asks for a school

Bangahan's barangay council passed resolutions, and the school division certified that no elementary school existed in Sitio Upper Rancho. Children from Upper Rancho, Lower Rancho and Dumalama walked up to 8 km along hilly farm roads, or paid for rides and boarding.

August 2018

A family offers land

Larry F. Ventura and Norma L. Ventura agreed to donate 2,655 square meters of their lot in Sitio Upper Rancho for the school. The local government later bought a full hectare from the Ventura family for the school site.

2018 – 2019

Plans drawn up

A feasibility study and operational plan set out Kindergarten to Grade 6 classes, one section per grade, for about 150 learners from the neighboring sitios.

September 29, 2020

Upper Rancho Elementary School opens

With PSDS Dr. Mercidita P. Apa-ap and Bangahan Integrated School Principal Igrosaper A. Binayao, the school opened its doors to the community.

School leaders through the years

The teachers who kept the school going.

While Upper Rancho is attached to Bangahan Integrated School, a teacher is designated School-in-Charge (SIC), or Officer-in-Charge (OIC), to run the school day to day. We honor each of them, and every teacher who stood in front of our learners.

2020 – 2022

The first years

The school opened on September 29, 2020 with the support of PSDS Dr. Mercidita P. Apa-ap and Bangahan Integrated School Principal Igrosaper A. Binayao. The Ventura family offered the land, and the local government funded the first two classrooms under Mayor Miguel Silva Jr. and Barangay Captain Remy Molina Jr. The Municipality of Pangantucan later bought the 1-hectare school site and donated it to DepEd.

Did you teach or serve here in these early years? Message us on Facebook so we can add your name.

2023 – 2025

Planning for six years

Under BIS Principal Dr. Ruth M. Evangelista, Teacher I Jhovien F. Gevero served as School-in-Charge. With teachers Dafny Joyce A. Hingpit (ICT Coordinator), Jasmin D. Magsayo (Reading Coordinator) and Flordemae C. Bayucot, the team wrote the School Improvement Plan 2023–2028. Mr. Gevero chaired its editorial board.

  • Mapped projects for reading, school safety, disaster readiness, technology and helping out-of-school youth return to class.
  • Ran fire and earthquake drills and planted trees on the campus.
  • Started the process for the LGU-funded two-classroom building. Construction began in 2026, and the classrooms are now in use.
  • Kept learners in school: 146 learners in 2023–2024 despite the school's distance and lack of funds.
2025 – today

Sir Darwin G. Don, OIC

Sir Darwin G. Don began his career in the Department of Education at Upper Rancho Elementary School. His first day of work in DepEd was here. One week later he was designated School-in-Charge (SIC), also called Officer-in-Charge (OIC), and he has led the school day to day since.

School Year 2025–2026 brought many firsts under his watch, working with Principal Dr. Maricel O. Alfeche, PTA President Jose Diano, Kagawad Marejoncil Maderse, the Bangahan barangay government and the Pangantucan local government: the Deed of Donation for the school site, the school's own electric meter and full electrification, a fire safety inspection, a stage built in 10 days, a graduation held on that stage, and the new LGU-funded two-classroom building, which his predecessor started and which is now in use.

As SIC he works hand in hand with the principal, the Pangantucan local government (LGU) and the Bangahan barangay government (BLGU).

Alongside running the school he teaches and advises Grade 4, coordinates guidance and child protection, led the Boy Scouts in 2025–2026 (3rd place at the camporal) and coordinated the School Improvement Plan 2026–2028. For School Year 2026–2027 he continues as OIC, working with new Principal IV Rey G. Samonte and PTA President Norma Ventura.

School Year 2025–2026

What the community built together.

  1. June – July 2025

    Safer paths and three formal requests

    Campus pathways were uneven and hard to walk. In July the school sent resolutions for a deed of donation, electricity from the barangay, and a backhoe to level the grounds and dig a garbage pit. The paths are now safe to use.

  2. August 2025

    Grade 4 parents repair the classroom

    The bamboo walls of the Grade 4 classroom had worn out. Parents and the adviser agreed to put their TV project aside and spend their contributions on repairing the room. Anti-bullying work also began, with monthly advocacy videos and guidance support for every learner involved.

  3. October 21, 2025

    Deed of Donation issued

    The Municipality of Pangantucan, which bought the 1-hectare school site from the Ventura family, formally donated it to the Department of Education. The land is now secure for the long term.

  4. November 19, 2025

    Fire safety inspection

    The school installed its own electric meter, improved wiring and added a fire extinguisher donated by the Administrative Officer.

  5. School year 2025–2026

    Scouts take 3rd place at the camporal

    Eight new scouts were trained. At the three-day camporal at Bangahan Integrated School, URES competed as the 5th patrol, placed 3rd overall and won Most Clean Camp and Most Discipline.

  6. March 2026

    The school has power

    With the PTA, teachers and the Bangahan barangay government led by Captain Butner Geron, the electrification project was completed and fully working.

  7. March 30, 2026

    A stage built in 10 days

    Led by Kagawad Marejoncil Maderse and PTA President Jose Diano, the community finished the stage in time for Year-End Rites on March 30.

  8. April 2026

    Parents agree on a child protection plan

    At the year-end General PTA meeting, 40 parent representatives signed a graduated sanction scheme for confirmed bullying, from a parent call-out to a review by the Child Protection Committee.

  9. May 6 – June 2, 2026

    ARAL Summer Program

    Four weeks of daily reading and math sessions for Key Stage 2 learners, with extra attention for those living far from school.

  10. 2026

    New two-classroom building now in use

    Funded by the Pangantucan local government and started in 2026, the building has opened and learners and teachers are using it. The project was first set in motion by Mr. Jhovien F. Gevero, our earlier School-in-Charge.

  11. School Year 2026–2027

    A community garden and more support

    A shared vegetable garden for learners and neighbors is planned for this school year. The school is also asking for internet, a watchman, repair funds, ICT equipment and printers.

School development

Building the school, one project at a time.

Our learners

Who we serve.

Most of our learners come from farming families in Upper Rancho and nearby sitios. Many families find it hard to cover school supplies, meals and health needs.

114learners enrolled today
27learners from 4Ps (Pantawid Pamilya) households
47learners enjoying the DepEd school feeding program
3Indigenous Peoples learners
2%dropout rate, mostly during the sugarcane harvest
8learners with learning disability manifestations*

Some pupils leave school during the sugarcane harvest. They work in the fields to earn food for their families and survive poverty. Our teachers and PTA keep reaching out so these learners can return.

* From our School Improvement Plan, SY 2025–2026.

How you can help

A growing school with no operating budget yet.

Upper Rancho Elementary School is attached to Bangahan Integrated School (BIS) and has no school ID of its own, so it has no MOOE. BIS pays our electric and water bills, which is a great relief. Our other funds have come from donations, so nothing is set aside for maintenance and repairs. We are praying for our own school ID and for all the privileges of a school promised by the Department of Education. Gifts of materials, labor or funds from the community, local government, private donors and organizations make a direct difference.
